notice: RN bank batch 141: Maternity case studies: meconium aspiration, late-preterm newborn, newborn discharge and postpartum hematoma. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that suggest meconium aspiration syndrome.

rationale.correct: Thick meconium with respiratory distress and air trapping is meconium aspiration.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each effect of aspirated meconium, indicate its mechanism.

rows.text: Air trapping and pneumothorax risk
Chemical pneumonitis
Atelectasis and stiff lungs
Barrel chest

rationale.correct: Meconium obstructs, inflames and inactivates surfactant.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: For a non-vigorous newborn with meconium, current guidance is to {{b1}}, and the newborn is at risk for {{b2}}.

options.text: start routine resuscitation with positive-pressure ventilation within the first minute
delay breathing support for tracheal suctioning first
stimulate for 3 minutes before any support
give naloxone first
persistent pulmonary hypertension
hyperglycemia
polycythemia only
jaundice only

rationale.correct: Ventilate promptly; watch for pulmonary hypertension.

perOption.b1:a: Routine suctioning below the cords is no longer recommended.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which parts of the NICU plan should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Pre- and post-ductal SpO2
Surfactant as prescribed
Minimal handling, warmth
Watch for pneumothorax
Frequent vigorous suctioning of the mouth and nose every hour
Start bottle feeding now to keep up the glucose

rationale.correct: Dual saturations, surfactant, minimal handling and air leak watch.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: NICU
exhibits.body: CPAP started. Chest x-ray: patchy infiltrates, hyperinflation.

questions.stem: Two hours later, review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Notify the provider at once
Prepare for needle decompression or a chest tube
Transilluminate the chest if ordered
Increase oxygen and wait to see if it settles
Bathe the newborn to remove the meconium

rationale.correct: Sudden deterioration with unequal breath sounds suggests pneumothorax.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Take action on a newborn pneumothorax.

questions.stem: On day 3, for each finding, indicate whether it shows improvement or needs follow-up.

rows.text: SpO2 95% on 30% oxygen
Chest tube draining with no air leak
Pre-ductal 96%, post-ductal 84%
Parents holding the baby skin to skin
Seizure-like movements of the arm

rationale.correct: Improving; shunting and seizures need follow-up.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that require action.

rationale.correct: Late-preterm newborns are at risk for breathing, temperature and glucose problems.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues in a late-preterm newborn.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate whether it fits transient tachypnea or respiratory distress syndrome.

rows.text: Cesarean without labor, fluid retained in the lungs
Surfactant deficiency in a preterm newborn
Ground-glass lungs with air bronchograms
Improves within 24 to 72 hours
Worsens over the first hours and may need surfactant

rationale.correct: TTN is retained fluid and resolves; RDS is surfactant deficiency.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The priority is {{b1}}, because cold stress {{b2}}.

options.text: warming and treating the low glucose
a bath
waiting for the next feed in 3 hours
discharge planning
raises oxygen and glucose use, worsening distress and hypoglycemia
has no effect on glucose
improves breathing
lowers metabolic rate

rationale.correct: Warm and treat glucose.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which interventions should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Skin to skin or a radiant warmer
Dextrose gel and a feed
Oxygen if SpO2 falls
Gavage feeds if RR stays high
Bathe the newborn now to remove the vernix and blood
Delay all feeding until 12 hours of age to rest the lungs

rationale.correct: Warmth, glucose, oxygen and safe feeding.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Plan
exhibits.body: Dextrose gel given. Recheck glucose in 30 minutes.

questions.stem: Before discharge on day 4, which teaching is especially important for a late-preterm newborn? Select all that apply.

options.text: Wake the baby to feed at least every 3 hours
Watch for yellow skin; late-preterm babies are at higher risk
Keep the baby warm with a hat and layers
Car seat challenge before discharge
Feed on demand only; let the baby sleep long stretches
Place the baby prone to sleep for better breathing

rationale.correct: Feeding, jaundice, warmth and car seat safety.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Take action with late-preterm discharge teaching.

exhibits.title: Day 4
exhibits.body: Breathing normally since day 1. Weight down 8%.

questions.stem: At the 48-hour follow-up visit, for each finding, indicate whether it is reassuring or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Six wet diapers and three yellow stools a day
Weight back to 7% below birth weight
Yellow to the abdomen, bilirubin 17 mg/dL
Temperature 36.8 C
Breastfeeding 8 to 10 times a day

rationale.correct: Feeding is good; the bilirubin needs treatment.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Highlight the finding that needs follow-up before discharge.

rationale.correct: A hip clunk needs evaluation; the others are normal.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues on the newborn exam.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate whether it is normal or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Caput succedaneum crossing sutures
Cephalohematoma not crossing sutures
Bulging anterior fontanel when calm
Absent Moro on one side
Pseudomenstruation in a female newborn

rationale.correct: Many newborn findings are normal variants.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The hip finding needs {{b1}}, and the most important safety teaching is {{b2}}.

options.text: an ultrasound and orthopedic referral
tight swaddling with the legs straight
no action
an x-ray in 5 years
safe sleep: alone, on the back, in a bare crib
using baby powder
avoiding all visitors
a daily bath

rationale.correct: Hip referral and safe sleep.

perOption.b1:a: Early treatment with a Pavlik harness.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which discharge teaching should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the cord stump clean and dry and fold the diaper below it
Petroleum jelly on the circumcision with each diaper change for a few days
A rear-facing car seat in the back seat
Call for a temperature of 38 C rectal or higher
Put alcohol on the cord three times a day
Remove the yellow film on the circumcision by scrubbing

rationale.correct: Cord care, circumcision care, car seat and fever.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Ultrasound
exhibits.body: Left hip dysplasia; Pavlik harness planned.

questions.stem: Which discharge tasks can the nurse delegate to the UAP? Select all that apply.

options.text: Check that the infant and parent ID bands match before the baby leaves
Take the newborn's vital signs
Teach the parents how to use the Pavlik harness
Assess the circumcision for bleeding and decide if it is normal
Help the parents carry belongings to the car

rationale.correct: UAPs do routine tasks; teaching and assessment stay with the RN.

perOption.a: Routine safety check with a protocol.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each statement by the parents, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "We'll keep the harness on all the time unless told otherwise."
"The baby will sleep in our bed so we can watch him."
"We'll put the car seat in the front so we can see him."
"Six wet diapers a day means he's getting enough."
"We'll give sponge baths until the cord falls off."

rationale.correct: Safe sleep and car seat teaching need reinforcing.
references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that suggest a hematoma.

rationale.correct: Severe pain and shock with a firm fundus and normal lochia suggest a hematoma.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of a postpartum hematoma.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate the most likely source of postpartum bleeding.

rows.text: Boggy fundus with heavy flow and clots
Firm fundus with a steady trickle of bright red blood
Firm fundus, normal flow, severe pain and swelling
Bleeding that slows with fundal massage

rationale.correct: Fundal tone and pain point to the source.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

options.text: notify the provider and apply ice to the perineum
massage the fundus harder
give an opioid and wait
sit the client on a hard chair
start an IV and prepare for drainage of the hematoma
discharge
encourage walking
give a laxative

rationale.correct: Notify, ice, IV and prepare for drainage.

perOption.b2:a: Large hematomas need incision and drainage.

references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: After the hematoma is drained, which postpartum medicines should the nurse plan to give before discharge? Select all that apply.

options.text: Rho(D) immune globulin within 72 hours
MMR vaccine for rubella non-immunity
Tdap vaccine
MMR during the next pregnancy instead
Skip Rho(D) because the baby is O positive like the mother's type

rationale.correct: Rho(D), MMR and Tdap postpartum.

perOption.d: Live vaccine is contraindicated in pregnancy.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
CDC/ACIP immunization schedules
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Day 1
exhibits.body: Hematoma drained in the operating room. Hemoglobin 8.6 g/dL, stable.

questions.stem: Which teaching should the nurse give with the MMR vaccine? Select all that apply.

options.text: Avoid pregnancy for 4 weeks after the vaccine
Breastfeeding can continue
Rho(D) immune globulin may reduce the vaccine's response; check immunity later
Mild fever or joint aches may occur
Stop breastfeeding for 2 weeks
No contraception is needed while breastfeeding

rationale.correct: Avoid pregnancy for 4 weeks; breastfeeding is safe.
references: CDC/ACIP immunization schedules
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Take action with postpartum vaccine teaching.

questions.stem: At discharge, for each finding or statement, indicate whether it shows recovery or understanding, or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Pain 3/10 with sitz baths
Voiding without difficulty
"I'll use condoms or another method for at least a month."
New increasing swelling and pain on day 3
Dizzy on standing with hemoglobin 7.2 g/dL

rationale.correct: Recovery; swelling or worsening anemia needs follow-up.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
